title: Traffic-slice A/B runbook for safe batching & cache recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a controlled A/B experiment across traffic slices to validate automated batching and KV-prefetch recommendations generated by the optimizer. We must quantify cost reduction, SLA impact (tail latencies and error surface), and signal quality regressions for downstream customers. Deliverables: experiment runbook, dashboard spec, sample-size calculations, preflight simulation results, and automated rollback/playbook for unsafe signal patterns.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end runbook in ops-runbooks with step-by-step traffic split and monitoring checks
2) Dashboard surfaces: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-request econ, cache-hit ratio, batch-size distribution, SLA breach rate, and anomalies flagged automatically
3) Statistical power >= 0.8 for primary metrics with sample-size justification per slice
4) Preflight traffic-replay sim shows <5% false-positive rollback triggers on historical traffic
5) Automated rollback circuit triggered by defined guardrail thresholds and validated in a smoke canary run
experiment_plan: Variants: control (current prod config), V1 (auto-batching heuristic only), V2 (auto-batching + prefix KV prefetch + short TTL), V3 (conservative batching + prefetch)

Traffic allocation: stratified by traffic-slice: high-QPS core, infrequent long-tail, authenticated enterprise customers; start with 1% total (distributed across slices), ramp to 10%/slice over 48h if safe
Duration: minimum 7 full days after ramp to capture diurnal and weekly patterns
Stopping criteria: clear statistical significance in cost or SLA metrics OR guardrail breach; proceed to progressive rollout only on passing slices

Power/sample sizing: target 80% power for detecting 5% reduction in cost/unit and 1.5x increase in p95 tail latency. Use stratified sample calculation per slice; expected sample sizes: high-QPS slice ~200k requests/day, long-tail slices require longer windows or pooled testing
Sequential analysis: use group-sequential monitoring with pre-specified looks at 24h intervals and alpha spending to avoid peeking bias
Confounder controls: pin model version, prompt template, and client SDK versions for duration of experiment
rollback_plan: 1) Immediate full traffic cutover to control for slices exceeding guardrails: set traffic_split to 100% control via rollout service
2) Automated alerting: PagerDuty escalation and channel #ab-safety with prefilled incident template
3) Post-rollback diagnostics: collect full traces, batch histograms, KV TTL evictions for 24h
4) Root-cause triage within 48h and retained snapshot of experiment config for replay
5) Optional: partial rollback (reduce variant to conservative config) when failures localized to small subset of clients
analysis_notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive prefetch reduces per-token cost but increases memory and eviction risk; must measure both econ and increased tail-latency probability
Decision thresholds: prioritize customer-facing SLA over marginal cost savings (SLA breach >0.5% triggers rollback), otherwise require >=10% cost improvement for enterprise slices before rollout
Long-tail strategy: pool sparse slices for statistical power but apply per-customer safety gates before any rollout
Bias considerations: routing differences (region, device, plan) can confound; use stratified randomization and post-hoc covariate adjustment
Future: incorporate bandit-style allocation once we have robust slice-level priors and automated safety gates
